# The Weaver's Dream

Long ago, the night sky was empty and dark. The Moon felt lonely in the vast emptiness, so she visited the Earth to seek companionship.

On Earth, she found an old weaver woman working by candlelight, creating beautiful tapestries with silver thread. The Moon watched, enchanted by the woman's skilled hands and patient spirit.

"Why do you weave alone in darkness?" the Moon asked.

"I weave to remember," the woman replied. "Each thread is a memory of someone I loved who has passed. When I weave them together, they live on."

Moved by this devotion, the Moon made an offer: "Come with me to the sky. Weave your memories where all can see them."

The woman agreed. The Moon lifted her and her silver thread to the heavens. There, the weaver began her greatest work, stitching memories across the darkness. Each knot became a star, each pattern a constellation.

When her work was complete, the old woman herself became starlight, scattered across her final tapestry.

Now, when we look up at night, we see the weaver's eternal work—countless stars connected by invisible threads, each one a memory shining bright against the darkness.

# The Weaver of Stars

Long ago, when the sky was empty and black, there lived a lonely weaver named Celeste who dwelt at the edge of the world. Each day she spun thread from moonbeams and wove blankets to keep the earth warm during the long nights.

One evening, Celeste's youngest daughter fell gravely ill. The child whispered, "Mother, the darkness frightens me. I wish I could see something beautiful when I close my eyes."

Heartbroken, Celeste worked through the night on her finest creation—a magnificent tapestry woven from silver thread, depicting all the hopes and dreams of humanity. When morning came, her daughter had passed peacefully in her sleep.

In her grief, Celeste climbed to the highest mountain and tore her tapestry into countless pieces, scattering them across the void. Each fragment caught fire from her sorrow and remained suspended in the darkness, burning eternally.

These became the stars—fragments of a mother's love, shining so that no child would ever fear the dark night again. And on clear evenings, if you look carefully, you can still see the patterns of Celeste's original tapestry, the constellations telling stories of hope across the infinite sky.
